questions.stem: How many square metres of canvas (approximately) will be required to make a conical tent 3 m high so that a man 2 m tall may stand anywhere within a radius of 1 m from its centre without stooping ?

PQRS is a square. M is a point on PS such that PM : MS = 2 : 1 and N is a point on SR such that SN : NR = 1 : 2. If the area of triangle MQN is 10 square units, then what is the perimeter of the square ?
A cubical wooden block of length 10 cm is sliced to produce a cross-section of maximum area. What is the area of the cross-section ?
In a triangle ABC, AD is the bisector of angle A that meets BC at D. If AB = 21 cm, DC = 20 cm and AB : AC = 3 : 4, then what is \(AC^2 - BD^2\) equal to ?
A square of maximum area is inscribed in an equilateral triangle. If the side of the triangle is equal to \((6 + 4\sqrt{3})\) cm, then what is the area of the square ?

A room is L m long, B m wide and H m high. Further, L > B > H and L, B and H are integers. The length of the longest pole that can be placed in the room is 17 m and the length of the longest pole that can be placed on the floor is 15 m. What is the volume of the room ?

questions.stem:
ABCD is a parallelogram with \(\angle ABC = 150^\circ\) and the sides have integer values. If the area of the parallelogram is 17.5 \(\text{cm}^2\), then consider the following statements :

I. It is possible to have a perimeter equal to 24 cm.

II. It is possible to have a perimeter equal to 72 cm.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
N number of cubes each of side length equal to 10 cm are joined end to end in a row. If the total surface area of the resulting cuboid is 3800 \(\text{cm}^2\), then what is the value of N ?

In a quadrilateral ABCD, \(\angle ABC = 90^\circ\) and \(\angle ACD = 90^\circ\). Let AB = p units, BC = q units, AC = r units, CD = s units, AD = t units, where \(p < q < r < s < t < 15\). If p, q, r, s and t are integers, then what is the area of the quadrilateral ?
